title: 1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER
summary: First weekly Saturday live stream, a 3.5-hour free-for-all Q&A covering training (imbalances, failure, dips, rib cage expansion, bulking, programming), nutrition, his injuries, and lots of life, anime, philosophy and dating questions. He announces Ko-fi based questions, program reviews and rotating stream themes (fitness, self-improvement, dating, philosophy).
claims: He does not count fiber or macros; he simply eats oats almost every day plus fruits and vegetables daily
He still takes bee pollen every single day because the benefits are too large to stop
An occasional beer or glass of wine will not kill your gains, but daily so-called moderate drinking is really an addiction and hurts hypertrophy since alcohol does nothing for you
He no longer believes in his earliest channel programs (the first full body and the Shaw-inspired one) because they had far too many sets; he was overzealous about volume
HIT with one or two sets is too little and German Volume Training too much; both sit at the extremes of the volume spectrum
For someone returning after a year off and 10 kg heavier, the Guts program is too much volume
To lose love handles lose weight; if they persist look at your diet. His side chunks stayed after losing 30 lb and only vanished when he dropped dairy and meat
He has avoided milk for three years and eats beef only about every two months because dairy made his body react badly
Lower back or SI-joint soreness during RDLs is not normal: it means you cue lower back instead of hip hinge, or your program overloads the low back so it never recovers
Training about 5 hours a week needs no lifestyle changes, it replaces Netflix and Instagram time, but do not center your whole life around the gym; that will not make you happy
Imbalances are normal: his right shoulder sits lower, travels more range on presses, does more work and is bigger; the favored, stronger arm on curls is paradoxically smaller because it works less
Correct an imbalance with 2-3 extra unilateral sets for the smaller side at the end of the workout, but accept it may never fully disappear because the body keeps favoring the strong side
Soreness is a poor indicator of a good workout since it peaks about 48 hours later; base workouts on performance and progression, not soreness

Minimalist, very intense training works for beginners or busy people, but maximalist training with isolation covering the whole body gets the most results; the gap is maybe 80 vs 100 percent, and that last 20 percent decides things at an advanced level
A great frame wants as little excess mass as possible, but a poor frame (narrow shoulders, wide hips) needs the extra size even at the cost of some fat to look big
With a wide waist: train delts for width, never skip core because people look there anyway, and build arms and legs so everything around the core looks bigger
Only someone with a huge V-taper can get away with small arms; without it you need massive arms

Despite the current consensus against icing, ice saved him every time with tendinitis: use reusable gel packs 10-15 min after training, then 5-10 min off, never longer (Tracy McGrady story of permanent damage)
With tendinitis, train around the pain rather than avoiding training altogether
He does not do static stretching; every loaded exercise he does is a weighted stretch
Brain fog after meals lasting over 30 minutes may point to overeating carbs or to gluten
The lat pulldown is the best pull-up substitute and is worth rotating in even if you can do pull-ups
He takes MSM daily: it helps tendon pain and makes nails and hair grow faster
After 15 years he found weighted dips are the chest/shoulder/triceps movement that fits his build best, letting him push the most load with the least pain; he never skips weighted dips and pull-ups
Dip slightly wider than shoulders on parallel bars; diverging bars push the shoulders into internal rotation and hurt
Creatine gives some people water retention but never caused him any adverse effect
Male aesthetic baseline: from the front the neck should be in line with the jaw; more than that looks intimidating, and longer necks need more work
A short, stocky lifter should not prioritise shoulders and mass for mass's sake, which makes him look stockier; focus on limbs and core development
Do both overhead press and lateral raises: the side delt is only an accessory mover in the press but the prime mover in raises, so they complement rather than cannibalize each other
Dips carry over a lot to bench since both are horizontal presses, but the best way to bench more is to bench
Zercher lifts are fun but there are better choices for hypertrophy
Teen lifters: take your time, never ego-lift, use 6-10, 8-12 and 10-15 rep ranges with some 5s, and train every body part semi-frequently; by 18-19 you will have a huge advantage
Anyone reaches a 225 lb bench eventually, but it means nothing; a number does not unlock a big chest, progression unlocks growth
As an advanced lifter, adding 0.2 inch to his arms in a year would already be a huge win
Your ability to work harder is limited by your ability to recover; to work harder, recover harder
Back movements aggravate triceps tendinitis because the elbow is extended under load; he feels it on straight-arm pulls
He is permanently bulking and has never tracked calories yet bulked successfully; tracking helps people who need regimentation and may be needed to get shredded
Rib cage expansion is real: the intercostal muscles grow; his rib cage section looks roughly double since his first pullover videos, a plus with a wide waist
Sleeping on your side and crushing an arm or shoulder can pinch nerves and eventually hinder growth
The reverse lunge as main leg lift is on paper a quad movement but in practice mostly glutes; do not bank on it to grow quads
10k steps a day gets people walking, but its promoters work in fitness and forget desk-bound workers cannot find the time
On weighted pull-ups he never goes to a dead hang, keeping the lats engaged as he teaches
Strength standards are stupid; at his size a 400 lb RDL is roughly early intermediate
Dumbbell pullovers on the floor limit the stretch, and on a bed the shoulder blades sink which is unsafe
Deadlift risk depends on your build and how you lift; he has never been hurt because he lets go of the bar before getting hurt
He went from eating meat twice a day to once a day or less with no loss of gains and felt better; reduce meat if curious but avoid extremes
Programming bench and overhead press: two upper days, each with a horizontal or vertical focus, e.g. open with dips then military press, or open with a seated press then flyes
To eat more, eat smaller and more frequent meals; one huge meal kills appetite for hours
Novices should lean heavily on the Smith machine vertical press because it handles stabilization and the bar path so they can just push
Zero reps in reserve fits isolation, presses, upper body and rows; never for good mornings, deadlifts or squats
Bodybuilders compete on a stage, not on implements, so use every tool: calisthenics, barbells, dumbbells, kettlebells, Smith machine
When starting kickboxing, combine it with lifting, go easy at first, then gradually shift time and energy toward it
He swapped bent-over dumbbell rows for chest-supported rows on a bench, though starting with bent-over rows helped build his posterior chain
Outer forearm grows with hammer-type curls; inner forearm with supination work and wrist curls
French fitness YouTube is about 15 years behind in science and practice; reading English content is an advantage
Shrugs are redundant for trap growth but are nearly free volume, so he uses them (and forearm work) to fill gaps in giant sets
He broke his big toe dropping a 45 lb plate, never saw a doctor and it healed crooked
At 20 years old and 120 kg, avoid calisthenics (joints) and powerlifting (slippery slope to staying fat); pick a balanced general resistance program, not Starting Strength
Training in prison where intensity is limited: bank everything on volume and frequency
With only a pull-up bar and dip bars, make weighted pull-ups and dips the staples and add cheap plates or a towel to isolate the arms
Rib cage expansion is intercostal muscle, not bone, so it shrinks if you stop training, just like the neck or any muscle
Rib cage expansion is unlikely without pullovers
A pillow-man physique with limbs bigger than the waist is impossible naturally and even on drugs
Super tight traps: keep the shoulders down, since stress makes you shrug to protect the neck; weighted trap stretches reinforce the pattern
Injury history: right knee (ACL) in football, left knee on squats, tendinitis, right shoulder twice on bench, broken ribs, broken wrist as a kid, all fully recovered
You cannot fully avoid shoulders on bench because the chest works through the shoulder joint
He never does 20+ reps; that is too far from a relevant intensity window
He bulks through winter and spring and maintains in summer when appetite is naturally lower
Preacher curls are a good staple for big biceps
He dropped Arnold presses not because they are suboptimal but because they no longer fit in the program
Finger push-ups are a waste of time for hypertrophy
Sleep apnea comes from fat around the chest and neck, not neck muscle
Martial artists who call bodybuilding vain confuse barbells with powerlifting and ignore that abs and biceps matter for their sport
If training performance drops while dieting, your deficit is too large; losing strength from weight loss is normal, from the deficit itself it is not
He refuses to coach; charging 500 USD a month to shuffle someone's program feels like a scam to him
Kids can start conservative training around 10 (goblet squats, pull-ups, push-ups) but should wait until 15-16 for heavy squats and deadlifts
Calves are not just genetics: his went from puny to two inches bigger in about two years simply by training them
Training arms and shoulders on lower days is fine as long as it does not hurt pressing on upper days
He takes only isolation and upper-body sets to failure, not every set
His least favorite trend: small naturals posting 'I look small in a shirt' photos, which blackpills others; real mass shows either way
Bulking is like growing hair out: the puffy in-between phase looks bad and many panic back into a lean physique, missing the good-looking end result
Vein position is genetic, but having visible veins is not
He trains every day from 6 pm until 8-9 pm
Tonnage is worth tracking so you do not become a volume or an intensity fiend; volume and intensity work together
Feeling drained after heavy deadlifts and squats is normal, he attributes it to blood sugar fluctuations
Inner glute pain from squats fixed for him by hip hinges that stretch the glutes
Olympic weightlifting lifts can be steered toward hypertrophy
For knots, roll on a lacrosse ball and use loaded stretching of the area, especially traps
To keep muscle on holiday, forget the diet, eat plenty and train whenever you can
Kelso shrugs, especially on the Smith machine, are very effective; Jefferson curls cost a lot of technique but build the posterior chain
Sit-ups built his abs the most
A natural can develop a body part until it looks enhanced, even if the same person on drugs would be bigger
The Toji program targets shoulders and traps and Guts targets arms; for big arms run Guts and add shoulder isolation
Women benefit just like men from using as many implements as possible
Protein powder is not worth the money at current prices
He does not recommend the Guts program to a returning lifter
Career advice: do not chase a dream job; take a comfortable job that pays enough and leaves time for hobbies and family
He learned English by watching shows daily before bed, first with then without subtitles
He never acts on his first instinct; he sleeps on decisions and refines them
To overcome shyness deliberately make conversations cringe and see that nothing bad happens
He started the channel after someone close died, realizing waiting until he looked better or knew more was pointless

best pull-up substitute, rotate with pull-ups
side delt is prime mover; do alongside overhead press
great overall delt builder, side delt only accessory
lower back soreness means bad cueing or overload
